title: Trauma Team Activation & Field Triage
keywords: level 1 SBP < 90 GCS < 9 penetrating torso tourniquet
level 2 flail chest 2 long bone fractures ejection fall > 20 ft
sources: Critical Vector — EM Pocket Guide: Trauma Activation (ACS-COT 2021, CDC Field Triage 2021)
ACS Committee on Trauma resources; CDC/ACS-COT Field Triage Guidelines (MMWR 2022)

changelog.change: Initial entry — 3-tier activation framework, CDC high/moderate-risk field triage, geriatric and paediatric adjustments, undertriage/overtriage targets.

summary: Undertriage is the dangerous error — when in doubt, activate up. In the patient ≥ 65, an SBP < 110 (not 90) already signals physiologic instability, and anticoagulation makes a minor mechanism dangerous. Children compensate until they crash — treat the mechanism and anatomy as the primary drivers.

items: Physiologic: SBP < 90 at any point; shock index > 1; absent radial/femoral/carotid pulse; GCS < 9 without sedation; airway compromise or a field intubation; paediatric SBP < 70 + (2 × age).

Anatomic: penetrating injury to neck/chest/abdomen/proximal extremity; open or unstable pelvic fracture; amputation proximal to wrist/ankle; suspected spinal cord injury; a prehospital tourniquet; major vascular injury.
Transfer: receiving blood products or > 1 L crystalloid for shock; intubated in transfer; acute decompensation en route.

Anatomic: flail chest / multiple rib fractures; open or depressed skull fracture; ≥ 2 proximal long-bone fractures; extremity trauma with an absent distal pulse or sensory deficit; burns > 20% BSA or an inhalation injury; GCS 9–13.
Mechanism: ejection; extrication > 20 min; death of another occupant in the same vehicle; high-speed impact; pedestrian struck; fall > 20 ft; motorcycle/ATV crash with separation; a seatbelt sign.
Special: age ≥ 65 with HR > 90 or SBP < 110; anticoagulated with a head or torso injury; pregnancy > 20 weeks.

body.text: MVC with rollover or > 12 in of intrusion; age > 65 with any concerning mechanism; a stable pelvic fracture; single-system injury with a high-suspicion mechanism; multisystem trauma not meeting Level 1/2; physician discretion.

items: HIGH-RISK (transport to the highest-level trauma centre): GCS ≤ 13; SBP < 90; RR < 10 or > 29; shock index > 1; any penetrating injury to head/neck/torso/proximal extremity; flail chest; ≥ 2 proximal long-bone fractures; crushed / degloved / mangled or amputated extremity proximal to wrist/ankle; pelvic fracture; open/depressed skull fracture; paralysis.

MODERATE-RISK (consider a trauma centre): falls > 20 ft (adult) or > 10 ft / 2–3× height (child); high-risk MVC (intrusion, ejection, death of an occupant, dashboard deformity); pedestrian/cyclist thrown or run over; motorcycle crash > 20 mph; plus age ≥ 65, anticoagulation/bleeding disorder, dialysis, pregnancy > 20 weeks, or EMS judgement.

body.text: Targets: undertriage < 5% (sensitivity ≥ 95%), overtriage < 50%. Geriatric pitfalls — normal vitals masking major injury (beta-blockers blunt the HR), baseline cognitive impairment masking a GCS change, low-energy falls causing intracranial haemorrhage on anticoagulation, and rib fractures causing respiratory failure over 24–48 h. Paediatric — age-adjusted SBP = 70 + (2 × age); vitals stay normal until decompensation.
